title: Positive depth of a finite boundary submodule of restriction sections
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and $V$ an affine open. Write $R=\mathcal O_L(V)$ and $P=(j_*(N|_U))(V)$ for $j:U\hookrightarrow L$. Let $S\subseteq P$ be a finitely generated $R$-submodule and $p$ a prime ideal of $R$. Set $y=h_V.\mathrm{fromSpec}(p)$, the corresponding point of $V$. If $y\notin U$, then $S_p$ is finite over $R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and has depth at least one [def-weil-pbc-depth], with depth infinity for zero modules.

source.place: Tag 0AVN (lemma-weakly-associated-direct-image), finite basic-open cover proof; Tags 01LC, 00LL

proof.text: Construct the finite localization witness from S.FG and Noetherianity of the affine ring. Apply exclusion of the maximal associated prime, then positive depth from that exclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0AVN, 00LL and 00LI, finiteness then associated-prime exclusion then depth

A finite submodule of sections pushed forward from an open has positive depth at primes outside the open

from.place: Depth >=2 extension paragraph: finite intermediate quotients in the boundary restriction surjectivity argument, before exhaustion by finite submodules. Boundary intermediate-submodule depth before the depth lemma.

lean.statement: theorem depth_one_affine_boundary_submodule {L : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian L] (U : L.Opens) (N : L.Modules) (hqc : N.IsQuasicoherent) (V : L.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (S : Submodule (L.presheaf.obj (op V)) (((Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj ((Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj N)).val.obj (op V))) (hS : S.FG) (p : Ideal (L.presheaf.obj (op V))) [p.IsPrime] (hy : hV.fromSpec ⟨p, inferInstance⟩ ∉ U) : ∃ hfinite : Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p S), letI := hfinite (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p S)
